findings.title: Unvalidated nb_blocks causes heap buffer overflow in argon2i_32
findings.evidence: argon2i_32 (c_monocypher.pyx:322) forwards the caller-controlled nb_blocks directly into crypto_argon2_config.nb_blocks (line 328) and sizes the work area as malloc((size_t)nb_blocks * 1024) (line 345) without enforcing the C API's documented requirement nb_blocks >= 8 * nb_lanes (monocypher.h:160). Inside crypto_argon2 the geometry is derived as segment_size = nb_blocks / nb_lanes / 4 and lane_size = segment_size * 4 (monocypher.c:752-754), so for nb_blocks = 0,1,2,3 with nb_lanes=1 lane_size rounds to 0, yet the initial fill loop still writes two 1024-byte blocks per lane at blocks[l*lane_size + i] (monocypher.c:776-781). For nb_blocks=1 only 1024 bytes are allocated but 2048 bytes are written (1024-byte heap overflow); for nb_blocks=0 malloc(0) is called and 2048 bytes are written. The same small counts make the final block pointer blocks + lane_size - 1 evaluate to blocks - 1 (monocypher.c:902), and store64_le_buf then reads 1024 bytes from before the allocation, folding that out-of-bounds heap memory into the returned hash (monocypher.c:911,918). There is no validation of nb_blocks anywhere in the binding, so any caller of the public Python API reaching argon2i_32 with nb_blocks < 2 triggers heap corruption (and nb_blocks 0..3 triggers the out-of-bounds read); upstream guards this with a 'nb_blocks must be >= nb_lanes*8' check that is absent here.
